description: A root URLconf that mounts by DOTTED STRING, against a source root that is not the repository root. This is the most ordinary thing a Django URLconf says and the engine could not follow it: the prefix table was keyed by string equality against the frontend's own module ids, so `include("billing.reports.urls")` matched a module only when the application's package root and the scanned root happened to be the same directory. plane's are not -- its sources are under `apps/api/` -- and every one of that application's 399 route declarations came to nothing: 51 entry points were enumerated against 399 declared (13%), and 31 of the 51 were the declarative fallback naming a class rather than a path. On this fixture the old resolution enumerated ZERO entry points and the analysis reported NO FINDINGS at all, while declaring OWASP ASVS 1.2.5 -- protection against OS command injection -- NOT EVALUATED. The command injection below is reachable only through the mount, and the negatives are the two shapes that look like one: a dotted string naming a module this program does not contain, which must mount nothing, and a handler in the same file that reads nothing a caller supplies.

expected.note: served at /api/v2/export/<pk>/; the prefix is in a file that names this module only as a string, and the module is one directory level deeper than the string says
